æcse, adsan, bil, byrse, scafan, sage, cimbiren, tigehoc, næfebor, mattuc, ippingiren, scear, culter and eac gadiren, siðe, sicol, weodhoc, spade, scofle, wadspitel, bærwan, besman, bytel, race, geafle, hlædre, horscamb and sceara, fyrtange, wæipundern.

Axt, Beil, Hippe, Bohrer, Hobel, Säge, Kimmeisen [Böttcherbeil], Ziehhaken, Naber [= Bohrer], Hacke, Brecheisen [?], Pflugschar, Kolter und auch Stachelstock, Sense, Sichel, Unkranthacke, Spaten, Schaufel, Waidhacke, Tragebahre, Besen, Stössel, Rechen, [Heu-]Gabel, Leiter, Pferdekamm und [grosse Wirthschafts-]Scheere, Feuerzange, Wage mit Gewicht;

Axe, adze, bill, borer, plane, saw, chime-iron [cooper's axe], drawing-hook, auger, mattock, crowbar[?], ploughshare, coulter and also goad, scythe, sickle, weed-hook, spade, shovel, woad-dibble, barrow, broom, beetle, rake, [hay-]fork, ladder, horse-comb and [large household] shears, fire-tongs, scales with weights;

Axe, adze, billhook, chisel, plane, saw, joining iron, hook for earthenware vessels, auger, mattock, crowbar, ploughshare, coulter, and also a goad, scythe, sickle, weed-hook (hoe), spade, shovel, woad-dibble, barrow, broom, mallet, rake, fork, ladder, horse-comb, scissors, fire tongs, weighing scale

ax, adze, billhook, chisel, plane, saw, clamp, pull hook, auger, mattock, crowbar, plowshare, coulter, and likewise a goad, scythe, sickle, hoe, spade, shovel, woad dibble, barrow, broom, mallet, rake, fork, ladder, horse comb and shears, fire tongs, scale.

note.seg: sic

Die ersten Wörter der Liste beginnen mit a-, b-; vgl. 17{c}.—Nicht ‘Schwert’ (Sweet, Kluge); vgl. Toller Suppl., noch jetzt bill: ‘Haumesser, Sichelhacke’; auch mengl.: Mätzner.—‘Axt, Krummaxt, Beil’ Sk-Wi
The first words of the list begin with a-, b-; cf. 17{c}.—Not ‘sword’ (Sweet, Kluge); cf. Toller Suppl.; still today bill: ‘chopper, bill-hook’; also ME: Mätzner.—‘axe, curved axe, hatchet’ Sk-Wi
So Sweet, Kluge; doch neben foratorium glossiert das Wort auch scalprum, scalpellum ‘Ahle [so Sk-Wi], Lanzette, Meissel, Gartenmesser’; s. Toller Suppl. s. v. byres
So Sweet, Kluge; but besides foratorium the word also glosses scalprum, scalpellum ‘awl [so Sk-Wi], lancet, chisel, pruning-knife’; see Toller Suppl. s. v. byres
‘joining-iron, clamp [Schraubzwinge]?’ Toller Suppl.; ‘edge-iron?’ Sweet; kimme, chimbe (mengl., chimb) ‘oberer Fassrand’; kimisern mndd. ‘Böttcherbeil’; Lübben. Fehlt Sk-Wi
‘joining-iron, clamp [screw-clamp]?’ Toller Suppl.; ‘edge-iron?’ Sweet; kimme, chimbe (ME, chimb) ‘upper rim of a cask’; kimisern MLG ‘cooper's axe’; Lübben. Not in Sk-Wi
‘Zughaken’ Kluge
‘draw-hook’ Kluge
Vgl. Kluge Etymol. Wb. s. v. naber. ‘Besen [?], Hacken, Harken [?]’ Sk-Wi
Cf. Kluge Etymol. Wb. s. v. naber. ‘broom [?], hoes, rakes [?]’ Sk-Wi
‘crowbar’ Toller, Sweet; cipping iren ‘Zimmerereisen’ (vgl. nengl. to chip) will emendieren Ritter o. 12³
‘crowbar’ Toller, Sweet; Ritter above 12³ would emend to cipping iren ‘carpenter's iron’ (cf. Mod. Engl. to chip)
Nicht ‘Pflugschar’, sondern das krumme Messer ‘Sech’ davor; vgl. Toller, auch Suppl.
Not ‘ploughshare’, but the curved knife in front of it, the ‘coulter’; cf. Toller, also Suppl.
So Kluge; vgl. jetzt goad; gadiren glossiert aculeus, stimulus
So Kluge; cf. today goad; gadiren glosses aculeus, stimulus
S. o. 10{q}. Noch jetzt spittle; mengl. spitel (Stratmann); ‘Waidpflanzer’ [?] Sk-Wi
See above 10{q}. Still today spittle; ME spitel (Stratmann); ‘woad-planter’ [?] Sk-Wi
‘barrow’ Toller Suppl., ‘wheelbarrow’ Sweet, ‘Schubkarren’ Sk-Wi, ‘Trage’ Mätzner, nicht mit Kluge ‘Korb’
‘barrow’ Toller Suppl., ‘wheelbarrow’ Sweet, ‘wheelbarrow’ Sk-Wi, ‘hand-barrow’ Mätzner; not, with Kluge, ‘basket’
Jetzt beetle ‘Schlägel, Rammstock’; ‘Hammer’ Toller Suppl., ‘Stampfe’ Kluge, ‘Schwinge’ Sk-Wi
Now beetle ‘mallet, rammer’; ‘hammer’ Toller Suppl., ‘stamper’ Kluge, ‘swingle’ Sk-Wi
Nicht ‘Gabel, fork’ im Sinne von furca Vinogradoff Villain. 170; jetzt gaffle ‘Mist(usw.)gabel’
Not ‘fork’ in the sense of furca, Vinogradoff Villain. 170; now gaffle ‘dung (etc.) fork’
Zum Scheren von Tieren und Pflanzen; Toller 824b
For shearing animals and plants; Toller 824b
Abbildung aus Agsächs. Kalender 11. Jhs.: Heyne Deut. Wohn. 34
Illustration from an Anglo-Saxon calendar of the 11th cent.: Heyne Deut. Wohn. 34
‘pair of scales’ Sweet; ‘steelyard’ Toller. Nicht ‘Gewicht’ (Kluge), obwohl pundar : perpendiculum glossiert; Toller. Mittelengl. punder: ‘Wage’
‘pair of scales’ Sweet; ‘steelyard’ Toller. Not ‘weight’ (Kluge), although there is the gloss pundar : perpendiculum; Toller. Middle English punder: ‘balance’
